subject: NimbleHealth renewal check-in — usage supply & term negotiation
messages:
From: Sara Wong <sara.wong@nimblehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baker <tomb@nimblehealth.com>; procurement@nimblehealth.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal check-in — usage supply & term negotiation

Thanks for the note, Sean — appreciate the proactive reach. We reviewed Q2 usage and there are a couple of items I want to surface before we jump to terms: 

- Token cadence: peak daily tokens have increased ~2.3x since May, but median latency is holding (see attached CSV sample).
- Latency: a handful of 95th percentile spikes on long chat sessions — Tom's flagged these for engineering.
- Procurement: we will need a clean SOW and a clear description of burst rights if we lock a 12-month commit.

Can we get a one-pager that summarizes: committed tokens, burst bucket, fallout SLA for spikes, and a projected monthly spend under two scenarios (flat growth, +30% growth)? If we can align that with pricing, procurement can move quickly.

Best,
Sara
Sara Wong
Head of Product, Integrations 
NimbleHealth

Attachments referenced: nimble_health_usage_q2.csv
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Wong <sara.wong@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal check-in — usage supply & term negotiation

Sara — thanks for the quick read. Attaching an initial snapshot and a short write-up below; Karthik and Monica looped to confirm pricing and SLA options.

Summary (high level):
- Current run-rate: ~1.6M tokens/day average in Q2; peak days ~3.8M.
- Baseline latency: 95th percentile across our hosted endpoints ~420ms for the model mix you're using; the attached SLA latency report has session-level examples.
- Proposed commit: 12 months, 40M tokens/month guaranteed; 20% burst buffer for sudden spikes (billed as pay-as-you-go beyond that).
- Discount framing: with the commit above, we can offer a 22% unit discount and a 30% credit back if monthly usage exceeds 110% of committed tokens for three consecutive months.

Action requested: confirm whether Nimble prefers (A) a 12-month commitment with burst buffer, or (B) a 6-month pilot with a higher per-token rate but smaller upfront commitment. Procurement note: for (A) we can provide a short SOW + DocuSign link once terms are agreed.

I'll attach the CSV and SLA PDF we referenced. If it's helpful, we can do a short screen-share this week to walk the dispatch/latency traces.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: nimble_health_usage_q2.csv; sla_latency_report.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sara Wong <sara.wong@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal check-in — usage supply & term negotiation

Following up with more detail on the economics and a small operational clarification. Sara, quick answers inline: 

- Pricing scenarios (monthly estimated cost):
  * Option A — 12m commit: 40M tokens/month at $0.0018/token => $72,000/mo (after 22% commit discount). Burst buffer (20%): billed at on-demand rate $0.0024/token.
  * Option B — 6m pilot: 25M tokens/month at $0.0022/token => $55,000/mo, no burst buffer commitment.

- ROI framing: based on your stated conversion uplift, we modeled a conservative 0.6% improvement in throughput that maps to ~$180k incremental ARR for Nimble on the current product line; with the 12m commit the payback period is ~3 months vs run-rate. (I can send the spreadsheet if you want the modeling.)

Operational ask: if we do (A), we need to pin a primary model for production (you currently route between two model families). Consistency lets us guarantee the latency tranche. Can Nimble confirm which family you want pinned for the committed traffic?

I'll prepare a redline-friendly SOW draft once you confirm option and model family.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference
From: Sara Wong <sara.wong@nimblehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, procurement@nimblehealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal check-in — usage supply & term negotiation

Appreciate the detail, team — this is helpful. Quick replies: 

- We prefer Option A (12m commit) if the burst buffer and SLA language can be explicit in the SOW.
- Model family: we want the lower-latency family pinned for committed traffic (the one labeled "rwd-lowlat-1" in your console). Tom will confirm the final internal sign-off this afternoon.
- Procurement: please send the SOW and DocuSign link; we will route the contract for signature once Tom confirms the pinned model.

Tom (cc'd) — can you confirm procurement timing? We are targeting end of next week to complete this.

Thanks,
Sara
